claims.claim: The thermodynamic minimum work to capture CO2 from air at ~400 ppm is about 20 kJ/mol (0.45 GJ per tonne, i.e. ~125 kWh/t) for 75% capture at 98% purity.
claims.episode_span: A rough calculation based on the free energy of dilution yields an energy floor on the order of twenty to thirty kilojoules per mole of carbon dioxide
claims.source_title: Direct Air Capture - Negative Emissions Technologies and Reliable Sequestration (NCBI Bookshelf)
claims.supporting_quote: Assuming an initial atmospheric concentration of CO 2 at 400 ppm at 25°C, the minimum work of capturing 75 percent of the CO 2 at 98 percent purity is 0.45 GJ/tCO 2 (20 kJ/mol CO 2 ).

claims.claim: Published direct air capture cost estimates span an order of magnitude, from $100 to $1,000 per tonne of CO2.
claims.episode_span: Direct air capture plants now spend hundreds to thousands of dollars to pull one ton of carbon dioxide out of the atmosphere.
claims.source_title: Direct Air Capture - Negative Emissions Technologies and Reliable Sequestration (NCBI Bookshelf)
claims.supporting_quote: The estimates found in the literature span an order of magnitude, from $100 to $1,000/tCO 2 ( Ishimoto et al., 2017 ).

claims.claim: Real DAC systems consume far more than the thermodynamic minimum: liquid-solvent systems use 8.2-11 GJ/t (thousands of kWh per tonne), an exergy efficiency of only 4-6 percent.
claims.episode_span: so the practical floor is higher but still measured in hundreds of kilowatt-hours rather than the thousands that current plants consume
claims.source_title: Direct Air Capture - Negative Emissions Technologies and Reliable Sequestration (NCBI Bookshelf)
claims.supporting_quote: Based on the energy requirements outlined for liquid solvent direct air capture systems, the “real” work is 8.2-11 GJ/t, leading to an exergy efficiency 8 of 4.1-6.2 percent.

claims.claim: Atmospheric CO2 concentration is roughly 400 parts per million (the 2024 global average was 422.8 ppm).
claims.episode_span: The concentration is only about four hundred parts per million
claims.source_title: Climate change: atmospheric carbon dioxide - NOAA Climate.gov
claims.supporting_quote: Based on the annual analysis from NOAA’s Global Monitoring Lab, global average atmospheric carbon dioxide was 422.8 parts per million (“ppm,” for short) in 2024, a new record high.

claims.claim: Solid-sorbent DAC has the same ~0.45 GJ/t minimum work but real work rates of 1.9-23.1 GJ/t, i.e. exergy efficiencies of 2-24 percent.
claims.episode_span: each cycle requires energy both to move enormous volumes of air and to regenerate the sorbent
claims.source_title: Direct Air Capture - Negative Emissions Technologies and Reliable Sequestration (NCBI Bookshelf)
claims.supporting_quote: Like liquid solvent systems, solid sorbent systems have a minimum work rate of 0.45 GJ/tCO 2 to capture 60-75 percent CO 2 from air to a 99 percent pure CO 2 stream. Based on the energy requirements outlined for solid sorbent systems, the “real” work rate is 1.9-23.1 GJ/tCO 2

claims.claim: Atmospheric CO2 measured at NOAA's Mauna Loa observatory peaked at just under 427 ppm (426.90 ppm) in May 2024 - consistent with the digest's 'about four hundred parts per million'.
claims.episode_span: The concentration is only about four hundred parts per million
claims.source_title: During a year of extremes, carbon dioxide levels surge faster than ever | NOAA
claims.supporting_quote: surged to a seasonal peak of just under 427 parts per million (426.90 ppm) in May, when CO 2 reaches its highest level in the Northern Hemisphere.

claims.claim: Global atmospheric CO2 rose from 365 ppm in 2002 to over 420 ppm in 2022 (NASA AIRS mid-troposphere measurements).
claims.episode_span: roughly four hundred parts per million and deliver it at one atmosphere
claims.source_title: Carbon Dioxide | Vital Signs - NASA Global Climate Change
claims.supporting_quote: Note the colors change as the amount of CO2 rises from 365 parts per million (ppm) in 2002 to over 420 ppm in 2022.

claims.claim: The theoretical minimum energy to extract CO2 from ambient air is commonly given as about 250 kWh per tonne of CO2, versus roughly 100 and 65 kWh/t for capture from natural-gas and coal plant flue gas.
claims.episode_span: translates to something like one hundred fifty to two hundred fifty kilowatt-hours per ton
claims.supporting_quote: Some authors give the theoretical minimum energy required to extract CO 2 from ambient air as 250 kWh per tonne of CO 2 , while capture from natural gas and coal power plants requires, respectively, about 100 and 65 kWh per tonne of CO 2

claims.claim: Direct air capture costs exceeded $1,000 per tonne of CO2 in 2025, driven by the small scale of deployment and energy factors.
claims.episode_span: Direct air capture plants now spend hundreds to thousands of dollars to pull one ton of carbon dioxide out of the atmosphere.
claims.supporting_quote: The current high cost of DAC is driven by the scale of deployment and energy factors. In 2025 DAC costs exceeded $1000 per tonne CO 2
